FeDril is currently a fixed-capacity SaaS, not an AI-token business. The production stack is approximately $284/month before customer-success labor. At 25 tenants with an 80% lightweight / 20% heavy mix, modeled compute is roughly $6 for a light tenant and $36–$39 for a heavy tenant, producing about 94% blended compute gross margin at $149/$399 pricing. A future GPT-5.4-mini-style workflow adds about $0.21 per light tenant and $4.05 per heavy tenant under the explicit token assumptions. The largest near-term unit-economics risk is unmetered usage and unproven capacity—not model-token cost.

Three reasons the naive pricing approach fails
A single $99 unlimited tier under-absorbs the always-on platform below roughly 10 customers and exposes margin to unmetered heavy usage.
Seat-based pricing alone misprices cost: storage, malware scans, PDF exports, and future AI actions are more correlated with compute than named users.
Quoting Advisor as available before multi-client packaging and usage enforcement are implemented creates operational, tenant-isolation, and margin risk.

Instrument per-tenant storage, uploads, scan duration, report/PDF generation, queue time, DB load, and egress.
Run load tests to replace the 50-weight-unit capacity-block assumption with measured saturation and scale triggers.
Separate production from the staging App Service plan or document a defensible COGS allocation and shared-failure tradeoff.
Implement server-authoritative usage meters before advertising hard limits or overage billing.
Track support, onboarding, and expert-review labor separately; compute GM is not total SaaS gross margin.
